headline: Methods operate on raw reads and pileups while profiling memory and throughput limits
label: Scalable Sequencing Data Computation
summary: New tools pair read-level inputs with measured compute behavior, from memory-bound mapping profiles to 10M-cell CPU workflows.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computation applied close to primary sequencing data, with attention to accuracy and efficiency. SomatiX uses allele-aware pileups from matched tumor-normal long-read data and is reported to outperform DeepSomatic. Cycle-Extractor casts ecDNA cycle reconstruction from short- or long-read breakpoint graphs as a MILP and is reported to outperform AmpliconArchitect and Decoil. scRM pretrains a single-cell foundation model on scRNA-seq reads instead of count matrices, reported as competitive. brisc runs a multithreaded CPU workflow on 10M cells in 3 minutes, reproducible across thread counts. The arXiv characterization of WGA, long-read, and short-read mappers with VTune and DAMOV-SIM identifies memory-bound functions and cache behavior. New here is the pairing of read-level or pileup inputs with explicit systems-level measurement; the items address distinct biological problems and share methodological concerns.
